DEX

Claiming airdrops

How to tell whether your wallet has a token airdrop, where to claim it on the DEX, and what to check before you confirm.

2 min read · Elysium testnet

How you know you have one

When the connected wallet has a token airdrop, the DEX link in the menu shows a small note under it: Claim airdrop once it is ready, or Check airdrop while Kalos is still checking. Kalos looks only at the wallet you are connected with, so connect the wallet that received the airdrop.

Claim it
Open DEX. Your airdrop appears at the top of the page as a card with the amount and the token.
Wait for Your airdrop is ready to claim. While the card reads Checking availability…, its button stays disabled.
Press Claim and confirm in your wallet. The dialog follows the transaction to Complete.
When it confirms, Kalos says Airdrop claimed. Tokens are in your wallet.
What happens behind the button

An airdrop is a fixed list of wallets and amounts. Before it asks your wallet, Kalos checks that the claim matches the connected wallet and the airdrop campaign, and the tokens go to that wallet. If you are connected with a different wallet, the claim is refused with “This claim does not match the connected wallet or campaign.”

Claiming is a transaction, so you need a little HYPE for the network fee. If you have none, get test HYPE first, as Getting started explains.

After claiming
The card disappears once the claim is recorded. An airdrop can be claimed only once.
The tokens show in your wallet panel and work on the DEX like any other token: you can swap them, deposit them in a pool or, for KALOS, stake them (Staking KALOS).
WHY IT MATTERS

Claims happen on the DEX page of Kalos, for the wallet the airdrop was made for. You never need to share anything with anyone to claim.

RISKS
Be wary of “airdrop” links in messages or on other sites that ask you to connect or sign. On Kalos, claim from the DEX page.
An airdrop claim never needs your seed phrase.
The amount is what was assigned to your wallet. Nobody can raise it for you.

GETTING STARTED

Getting started on the Elysium testnet

Connect a wallet, get free test HYPE from the faucet and learn what testnet means: nothing here has real value.

2 min read · Elysium testnet

What testnet means

Kalos runs on the Kinetiq Elysium testnet, chain ID 99801. A testnet is a practice network, and the banner at the top of every page says it plainly: NFTs and HYPE have no real value. You can try every feature, make mistakes and start again without losing real money.

HYPE is the network’s own token. It pays the small network fee, called gas, of every transaction, and it is the currency most prices on Kalos are shown in.

Connect your wallet
Press Connect wallet at the top right. On a phone, open the account menu (the person icon at the top right) and press Connect wallet there.
Choose your wallet in the list. You can search for it by name.
Approve the network request in your wallet. Kalos asks it to switch to Elysium testnet, and to add the network as Kinetiq Elysium Testnet if your wallet does not know it yet.
Your balance now shows in the header. Press it to open your wallet panel.

If your wallet says it cannot add the network, use a wallet that supports custom networks.

Get test HYPE

You need a little HYPE before you can do anything on chain. Test HYPE is free:

Get test HYPE in the testnet banner opens the official Elysium faucet
(opens in a new tab)
↗ in a new tab. On a phone it is also under More, as Faucet.
In your wallet panel, Get HYPE opens the bridge, which moves HYPE from HyperEVM testnet to Elysium. On testnet the faucet is listed there too.
Sign in to Kalos

Some features use your Kalos account instead of a transaction: posting on Social, a profile with a username, feedback. Sign in to Kalos in the account menu opens a dialog. There, Sign in asks your wallet to sign a message. It is free: no transaction, no gas. If you are new, choose New to Kalos? Create your profile in the same dialog to pick your username.

What every transaction costs

Swaps, deposits, listings, purchases, offers and mints are transactions. Each one pays a network fee in HYPE, so always keep some HYPE aside. The Max buttons help: Max for HYPE on the DEX keeps an estimate of the network fee, and Max in Wrap HYPE keeps 0.002 HYPE for gas.

Each transaction opens a dialog that follows it from Sign to Confirming to Complete. When it is done, the result is in your wallet.

WHY IT MATTERS

Practising on testnet is the safest way to learn how wallets, approvals and reviews work before real money is involved.

RISKS
Test HYPE and testnet NFTs have no real value. Nobody needs to sell you test HYPE: the faucet gives it away.
A transaction you confirm is final once it is confirmed, even on testnet. Read every review before you confirm. Staying safe explains what to check.
